newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Big volumes weaken Colombo low grown tea prices.
newsitem.headline: Big volumes weaken Colombo low grown tea prices.

text.p: Low grown tea prices fell at the Colombo auction as buyers held back because of the big volumes on offer, brokers said on Wednesday.

"Low growns fell because huge quantities are on offer in the next couple of sales," said a Forbes and Walker tea broker. "The November-December backlog was cleared by putting it in the February sales. So there's no hurry for buyers to pick up tea."
The anticipated average price for the 5.1 million kg on offer rose to about 105.75 rupees per kg ($1.83) from 104.73 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.

Most low growns were between five and 10 rupees lower but brokers said prices of all other types of tea rose, with better Western BOPs and BOPFs four to six rupees dearer and improved Nuwara Eliyas rising even more.
The next auction is on February 18-19 with 6.2 million kg on offer.
